title: From Rationale to Testable Hypotheses
description: AIL 606 textbook section on converting a design rationale into a falsifiable usability hypothesis with four parts (named mechanism, observable outcome, direction, and a threshold a small sample could plausibly miss), calibrating the threshold against sample size, and deciding whether a result revises the prototype or the rationale.

learning_objectives.statement: Convert a design rationale into a falsifiable, directional hypothesis with an observable outcome and a stated threshold
Distinguish a prediction the session can disconfirm from a goal it can only restate
Ground each hypothesis in a named mechanism (for example, an extraneous-load reduction) so the test checks a theory, not a preference
Decide when a result should revise the design and when it should revise the rationale

alignment_method: deterministic lexical mapping v2 with direct-evidence fallback; instructor review required
